title: The Day a Protection Claim Is Measured From
content:
Every claim under Pass and Trip Protection is measured from a single day, settled from the papers accepted on
it and the day the claim was made.

1. Where a paper accepted on the claim reached the collective after the day the claim was made, the claim is
   measured from the day the last of the papers accepted on it reached the collective.
2. Where every paper accepted on the claim reached the collective on or before the day the claim was made, the
   claim is measured from the day the claim was made.
3. In every other case the claim is measured from the day cover began.

**What separates the three.** The first two turn on there being at least one paper accepted on the claim; the
third is the case in which no paper stands accepted on it at all. Between the first two the question is
whether the last accepted paper reached the collective after the day the claim was made or on or before it; a
paper reaching the collective on the very day the claim was made falls on the second, not the first.

**Illustrations (hypothetical inputs).** A claim made on a day with a doctor's certificate accepted eight days
later: the claim is measured from the day that certificate reached the collective. A claim made on a day with
a certificate accepted three days earlier and nothing since: the claim is measured from the day the claim was
made. A claim made on a day with two papers accepted, one before it and one after it: the later one is the
last accepted, so the claim is measured from the day that one reached the collective. A claim on which no
paper at all stands accepted: the claim is measured from the day cover began.
